messages:
maria: Heads up — builds for some Dedicated console customers are failing when the SDKs pull in the new telemetry package. Started after redwood-telemetry bumped to 3.x. Can we discuss mitigations?
kevin: Oof. Which signal is failing exactly?
sam: Repro would help. any stack traces?
maria: webpack errors in console bundle: "Duplicate identifier 'TelemetryClient'" and bundler hanging. gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro-telemetry-bundle
julie: Quick options off top of head: 1) make telemetry an optional/peer dep and document it, 2) add a small compatibility shim that normalizes v2/v3 APIs, 3) vendor telemetry in console for now to force single version.
kevin: I prefer a shim we control. Keeps the SDK API stable and avoids pinning console forever.
sam: For JS/TS bundlers, peerDependency + shim feels right. For Python we can do an extras_require like `redwood-sdk[telemetry]` but lazily import so plain `pip install redwood-sdk` doesn't break.
maria: lazy import + no-op fallback would solve runtime for py. JS still painful because bundlers include transitive deps at build time.
julie: Could we publish a tiny package `@redwood/telemetry-shim` that re-exports v2 API but adapts v3 under the hood? SDKs depend on the shim (semver-stable), console can pin the concrete telemetry implementation during build.
kevin: That works. TS approach: declare `@redwood/telemetry-shim` as a dependency of SDK but mark `redwood-telemetry` (concrete impl) as a peerDependency so console or host can provide whichever version it needs.
sam: For python: create `redwood_telemetry_shim` on PyPI that exposes the same small API surface and imports either telemetry_v2 or telemetry_v3. Setup extras: `pip install redwood-sdk[telemetry]` pulls in shim and preferred impl.
maria: Also need a short-term stopgap: vendor telemetry in our hosted console build to unblock customers while we ship the shim. That buys time for semver-safe shims.
julie: agree. We'll add a webpack alias in console canary for `redwood-telemetry` -> `@redwood/telemetry-shim` until clients upgrade.
kevin: Tests: add a bundling integration test in CI that simulates console build with multiple telemetry versions. Catches this class of regression early.
sam: I'll file three issues and PR skeletons: TS shim, Py shim, console alias + CI test.
maria: rough release plan: 1) publish shims (patch releases) 2) canary console with alias 3) SDK minor bump to depend on shim 4) roll clients over 2 weeks.
kevin: timeline seems OK. Need to mark as opt-in telemetry until we've verified no perf regressions.
julie: small nit — for TS, peerDependency warnings can be noisy. We should provide clear install docs and automated script `tools/resolve-telemetry.sh` for integrators.
sam: good call. I'll add an onboarding snippet and an npm alias example:```json
// package.json (consumer)
"dependencies": {
  "@redwood/telemetry-shim": "^1.0.0",
  "redwood-telemetry": "^3.0.0"
}
```
maria: Devex checklist: - publish shims (sam/kevin) - console canary alias (julie) - CI bundle test (julie) - docs & install snippet (sam) - notify support & CSE (maria)
devex-bot: deploy-canary started for console (canary-42) :rocket:
infra-bot: NOTE: pinning in customer repos will create long-tail support. Recommend we ship shim PRs within 48h and vendor only as emergency rollback.
maria: Agreed. I'll coordinate with support to notify customers and schedule the canary. Thanks all.
kevin: I'll take the py shim PR. Sam -> TS shim, Julie -> console + CI.
maria: assigning now and will follow up in weekly rollout check. @devex-bot please remind in 7d about the rollout checkpoint :thumbsup:
